title: Man. Post. Cap. II: Posterior quaestio de poena — distinguish; Adam separate; proprie/improprie
pass_a_gloss: The posterior question concerning the penalty of this imputed sin itself also desires some explanation. First, however, penalty must be distinguished; then Adam must be separated from us. Penalty is said either properly or improperly. Properly again in many ways: but there is no need to enumerate all the kinds of penalties which I think you know, for that would be both long and useless to the matter we are treating. It is enough to hold in what sense hereditary corruption is called a penalty by you and by our other brothers, whose opinion you wish to defend against me.
pass_b_english: Before we go further, the later question on the penalty tied to this imputed sin needs clearing. Two moves first: sort out what penalty means, and keep Adam distinct from us. Penalty can be named properly or improperly, and even the proper sense branches many ways. I will not catalogue every species you already know—that would be long and beside our point. Hold only the sense in which you and the other brothers whose case you defend against me call hereditary corruption a penalty.
source_text: Posterior quaestio de hujus peccati imputati poena etiam ipsa aliquam explicationem desiderat. Primum autem poena distinguenda est; deinde separandus a nobis Adamus. Poena dicitur vel proprie, vel improprie. Proprie rursus multipliciter: sed nihil opus est omnia poenarum genera quae te nosse arbitror, enumerare, id enim cum longum esset, tum ad rem quam agimus inutile. Satis est tenere quo sensu corruptio haereditaria poena dicatur a te aliisque fratribus nostris, quorum sententiam adversus me tueri vis.

choices.choice: Distinguish poena; separate Adam; hold brothers sense of hereditary corruption as poena
